items.summary: The Pistons will be without sharpshooter Duncan Robinson for at least the next few games. The team announced today (via Twitter) that Robinson has been diagnosed with a left quadriceps strain after exiting Saturday’s game vs. Miami with what was initially referred to as left thigh soreness. The plan, per the Pistons, is to reevaluate Robinson in one week. That means he’ll miss games vs. San Antonio (Tuesday), New Orleans (Wednesday), Toronto (Friday), and Atlanta (Sunday) before potentially being checked out prior to next Tuesday’s contest in Orlando. Robinson has played a key role for the 8-4 Pistons so far this season, scoring double-digit points in every single one of his 12 outings and averaging a career-high 17.4 points per game while converting 43.1% mark of his 9.1 three-point attempts per contest. items.summary: Veteran NBA wing Haywood Highsmith will suit up for Team USA during the upcoming window of World Cup qualifying games, agent Jerry Dianis tells Hoops Rumors. Highsmith, who is currently a free agent, has appeared in 225 total regular season games since making his NBA debut in 2019. The versatile 29-year-old swingman enjoyed his best years in Miami, including a 2024/25 season in which he averaged 6.5 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 1.5 assists in 24.6 minutes per game and posted a .458/.382/.721 shooting line over the course of 74 outings (42 starts). items.title: Jazz Waive Trey Alexander
items.summary: The Jazz have waived Trey Alexander, who was on a two-way contract, according to a team press release. Releasing Alexander will create a roster opening for Jonas Aidoo, who will reportedly sign a two-way deal with Utah. Alexander entered the 2024 draft as an early entrant after three college seasons at Creighton. He didn’t hear his name called during that year’s draft, but he quickly signed a two-way contract with Denver and spent his rookie campaign with the Nuggets. The 23-year-old guard didn’t return to Denver in 2025/26, instead signing a two-way deal with New Orleans in July 2025. He became a free agent again this past summer, when he signed his two-way pact with the Jazz. Alexander has put up big numbers in the G League over his first two-plus seasons but hasn’t played much at the NBA level. items.title: Killian Hayes To Sign With Barcelona
items.summary: Free agent guard Killian Hayes is heading to Spain to sign with Barcelona, his agent Yann Balikouzou tells Michael Scotto of HoopsHype (Twitter link). Hayes’ contract with Barca features an NBA opt-out clause, Scotto reports. The seventh overall pick in the 2020 draft, Hayes was a Piston for most of his first four NBA seasons before being waived in February 2024. After he was unable to find another NBA opportunity, Hayes spent the 2024/25 campaign in the G League with the Long Island Nets aside from a brief 10-day deal with Brooklyn. Hayes returned to the NBAGL last season, suiting up for the Cleveland Charge, until he signed a pair of 10-day contracts and then a two-year, minimum-salary deal with Sacramento during the last couple months of 2025/26.
